copy from lynq-ml the pieces every service shares: resources/log_config.json printing the request uuid on each log line, exception_handlers.py, logging_context.py, middleware/request_uuid.py with EXEMPT_PATHS pointing at /lynq-agent/health, and response/models.py with the GlobalRestResponse envelope
lay out the src/ tree the service will grow into: db/, model/, agent/ with graph, tools, callbacks, context and language, plus prompt/, llm/, client/ and router/
check the module comes up with docker compose and that GET /lynq-agent/health answers

write the Dockerfile on the same python base image as lynq-ml, with no Pango/Cairo, installing requirements.txt with --require-hashes, running as a non-root user, serving uvicorn src.main:app on 0.0.0.0:8090 and with a HEALTHCHECK hitting /lynq-agent/health
add a .dockerignore leaving out tests, .venv, __pycache__, migrations/versions/*.pyc and .git, and a .gitignore for the module

add the VERSION file, a README for the module explaining how to run it and which environment variables it reads, and the skeleton of tests/ with its conftest
add the lynq_agent_db database to mysql-init/init.sql so a fresh mysql container comes up with the agent schema already created

create conversation table in the liquibase changelog file 00-initial-schema.sql. columns: id [string 36], short_id [int, auto increment, unique], user_id [string 64], job_id [string 64], base_resume_id [string 64], job_snapshot [JSON], base_resume [JSON], language [string 8], resume_language [string 8], status [string 32, AWAITING_CONFIRMATION|ACTIVE|RUNNING|APPLIED|EXHAUSTED|ABANDONED], run_token [string 36, nullable], llm_provider [string 32], llm_model [string 128], input_price_per_1m [decimal 10,4], output_price_per_1m [decimal 10,4], max_turns [int], max_steps [int], turn_count [int, default 0], applied_resume_id [string 64, nullable], llm_calls [int, default 0], total_prompt_tokens [bigint, default 0], total_completion_tokens [bigint, default 0], cost_usd [decimal 16,8, default 0], created_on [datetime], updated_on [datetime]. indexes on (user_id, created_on), (status, updated_on) and (created_on). money is decimal, never float

add message table to the changelog. columns: id [string 36], conversation_id [string 36], seq [int], role [string 16, user|assistant|system], content [text], turn_key [string 36, nullable, client side idempotency key], warnings [JSON, nullable], created_on [datetime]. unique (conversation_id, turn_key) and (conversation_id, seq). foreign key conversation_id -> conversation.id

add resume_version table to the changelog. columns: id [string 36], conversation_id [string 36], version [int], resume [JSON], changes [JSON], produced_by [string 36, nullable, the message that produced it], is_current [boolean], created_on [datetime]. unique (conversation_id, version). foreign key conversation_id -> conversation.id

add trace_span table to the changelog. columns: id [string 36], conversation_id [string 36], message_id [string 36, nullable], parent_id [string 36, nullable], step [int], kind [string 24, llm|tool|thought|limit|error], name [string 64], input [mediumtext, nullable], output [mediumtext, nullable], prompt_tokens [int, nullable], completion_tokens [int, nullable], cached_prompt_tokens [int, nullable], cost_usd [decimal 16,8, nullable], latency_ms [int, nullable], error [text, nullable], created_on [datetime with milliseconds]. index on (conversation_id, created_on). no foreign key: the spans of a failed turn outlive the message that was rolled back

map the four tables as SQLAlchemy 2.0 models in src/db/models.py, with an async engine and an async_sessionmaker in src/db/session.py reading DB_URL, plus a test that no column drifted between the models and the changelog

run the liquibase changelog on startup: src/db/migrations.py turns DB_URL into a jdbc url and shells out to liquibase update, wired into the lifespan of main.py behind DB_MIGRATE_ON_STARTUP, with liquibase and a jre bundled into the image. the credentials go through the environment, never on the command line, and the tables in the changelog stay unqualified so DB_URL decides which database is migrated

add scripts/export_eval_corpus.py: dump the (job posting, base resume, tailored resume) triples to JSONL for the thesis corpus, dropping personal_info and hashing the candidate id with EVAL_CORPUS_SALT

build an endpoint in lynq-agent whose signature is POST /lynq-agent/dmz/conversation { job: { id, title, company, description, workType, skills }, baseResumeId, baseResume, language, resumeLanguage }: it opens a conversation over a job posting and a base resume, freezes both on the row and answers { conversationId, greeting, status } inside the GlobalRestResponse envelope, demanding the lynq-request-uuid and user-id headers

build an endpoint in lynq-agent whose signature is POST /lynq-agent/dmz/conversation/{conversationId}/turn { message, turnKey }: it runs one exchange of the conversation and answers { reply, resume, changes, warnings, version, status, turnsLeft }

build an endpoint in lynq-agent whose signature is GET /lynq-agent/dmz/conversation/{conversationId}, with no body: it answers the status, the whole thread, the resume in force and the list of versions, so the modal can be reopened and the conversation inspected by hand

build an endpoint in lynq-agent whose signature is PATCH /lynq-agent/dmz/conversation/{conversationId}/applied { appliedResumeId }: lynq-bff calls it after applying and it closes the conversation, answering { status }

write a client for lynq-ml in lynq-agent that extracts the skills of a job posting exactly once, when the conversation is created, and freezes the answer into job_snapshot.extractedSkills; the snapshot shape is final even though the call can be stubbed, and if lynq-ml is unreachable the conversation still opens with the skills the posting already declares

the language a resume is written in arrives in the request, read from the candidate resume record, and lynq-agent stores it exactly as it arrives: run langdetect over the summary and the work experience descriptions only as a check and log a WARN with both values when they disagree, never falling back to the UI locale, because a UI in English over a resume in Spanish would make the agent translate the resume
truncate the job description to AGENT_JOB_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS, 6000 by default, before freezing the posting into the conversation snapshot in lynq-agent
write the repository of lynq-agent over the four tables: create_conversation, load_for_turn selecting FOR UPDATE, append_message, save_version, save_spans and mark_applied

implement the first transaction of a turn in lynq-agent, which has to take milliseconds: SELECT the conversation FOR UPDATE, reject with 409 a RUNNING turn newer than AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT and take over an older one as a dead process, reject with 409 an EXHAUSTED conversation or one whose turn_count already reached max_turns, answer 403 when the user-id header is not the owner, flip the row to RUNNING with a fresh run_token, insert the user message and commit before touching anything expensive

make a turn in lynq-agent idempotent by turn_key: replay the stored answer only when the assistant message exists, and when only the user message is there, the orphan of a process that died mid-turn, reuse that row and run the turn again instead of replaying an answer that was never produced

implement the second transaction of a turn in lynq-agent: SELECT the conversation FOR UPDATE and compare the run_token, and when it no longer matches treat this process as a zombie another turn superseded, delete its orphan user message, write a trace span named stale_run and answer 502 without persisting anything else; otherwise insert the spans, insert the new resume version flipping is_current, insert the assistant message and update turn_count, the status which becomes EXHAUSTED once turn_count reaches max_turns, run_token back to null and the cost rollup, all in the same commit

implement the error path of a turn in lynq-agent: delete the user message so a retry with the same turn_key runs again instead of colliding with the unique key, leave the conversation ACTIVE with a null run_token and turn_count untouched, dump the spans the handler accumulated before the cut with a null message_id plus a final span of kind error, and answer 502; a failed turn must not cost the candidate a turn

give every 409 of lynq-agent a code in the envelope so the front can tell them apart: TURN_IN_PROGRESS, CONVERSATION_EXHAUSTED and ALREADY_APPLIED; and make the applied endpoint idempotent, answering 200 when it is repeated with the same appliedResumeId and 409 when it arrives with a different one over an already applied conversation

kill the lynq-agent process by hand between the two transactions of a turn and verify the rescue: the conversation is left RUNNING with an orphan user message, a new turn is rejected with 409 while AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT has not passed, and once it has the next turn takes the conversation over and reuses that orphan message

verify the lynq-agent checkpoint against a real MySQL: a curl creating a conversation plus two turns has to leave coherent rows in the four tables, and the queries in docs/queries.sql have to show the conversation, the thread, the trace of each turn, the resume versions and the cost rollup in full
add cryptography to the lynq-agent lock: aiomysql cannot authenticate against MySQL 9 without it, since caching_sha2_password needs the RSA step

start the LLM work with tests/test_structured_output.py: a real turn has to close with the TurnAnswer tool call, so we verify that nova pro honours tool_choice=any instead of assuming it; if it does not, the fallback is dropping response_format, asking for the JSON in the prompt and validating it with pydantic plus one retry

add src/llm/factory.py that builds ChatBedrockConverse with the model id, region, max tokens and temperature 0 when LLM_PROVIDER is bedrock, and ChatOllama with qwen2.5:7b when it is not, reading everything from the environment

write src/agent/graph.py with langchain.agents.create_agent over the tools find_evidence and apply_edit, the system prompt rendered from a jinja template per provider and response_format=TurnAnswer with reply and warnings, and pass recursion_limit = 2 * max_steps + 6 as the hard cap so the soft cap of the tools always fires first
wrap the ainvoke of the loop in asyncio.wait_for with AGENT_TURN_TIMEOUT minus 30 seconds, so a turn kills itself before another process can declare it dead and take the conversation over

add find_evidence(claim) to src/agent/tools.py: a lexical search in code over the base resume returning path and matched, normalised without accents or symbols, by prefix for claims of four characters or more and by exact word for the short ones like Go, C#, AWS, SQL or Git, and never looking at personal_info

add apply_edit(section, op, payload) to src/agent/tools.py answering OK or REJECTED with a literal reason: personal_info is immutable, no new entries in work experience or education, dates are immutable, and skills only with the textual matched that find_evidence returned in this same turn; plus a langdetect check bounded to prose longer than 80 characters once the skill names are removed, rejecting only when the detected language is the one the agent talks in and not the one the resume is written in

add src/agent/callbacks.py with a TraceCollector that keeps the spans in memory until the second transaction, reads the tokens from the usage_metadata of the message instead of estimating them, and counts the steps: once max_steps is spent the tools answer STEP LIMIT REACHED and a span with kind=limit is written

do not store the whole system prompt in the LLM span: keep the messages of the turn plus the resume_version_id and the hash of the template, which is enough to rebuild it, since the resume is already in resume_version and the posting in job_snapshot

put the turn context in contextvars in src/agent/context.py, with the base resume, the current resume, the run token, the step counter and both languages, so the tools read it per request and nothing lives as module state

split personal_info out in code before rendering the prompt and attach it back when each version is serialized: the model must never receive the name, the contact details or the links of the candidate

keep a price sheet of input and output USD per million tokens per model in the code and copy it onto the conversation when it is created; a model that is not in the sheet costs zero and logs a warning instead of bringing the turn down
unwrap the JSON when the model answers with text instead of the tool call, so the candidate never reads a raw {"reply": ...} in the chat
make the resume of the turn response come from the last resume_version left by apply_edit and never from the text of the model, which only contributes reply and warnings
add tests/test_react_loop.py running with AGENT_MAX_STEPS=2: the turn has to end in a valid partial answer with its kind=limit span, not in a 502

run a real turn end to end and check the checkpoint: the loop produces edits on the resume and leaves trace_span rows with every step, their tokens, their latency and the cost rollup on the conversation

write the system prompt of the resume tailoring agent as resources/prompts/resume_tailor/ollama.jinja and bedrock.jinja, fully in English with no Spanish in it, and with {{ language }} and {{ resume_language }} as the only language variables

in the system prompt, allow only reordering, prioritising and rewriting what the resume already backs, and make the agent call find_evidence for every skill the posting asks for and the resume does not list before deciding anything about it, listing the gaps it finds no evidence for in the reply instead of covering them

in the system prompt, forbid adding jobs, degrees, dates or skills that are not in the resume, and make the agent refuse, explain why and offer the real alternative when the candidate asks it to invent something
keep the LyNQ score and any other score out of the system prompt: the agent adapts the resume, it does not optimise a number
in the system prompt, make the agent write its reply and warnings in {{ language }} and every string it passes to apply_edit in {{ resume_language }}, and never translate the resume

in the system prompt, make a skill enter the resume with the wording find_evidence returned and never the wording of the posting, and have the agent say so in the reply when the posting names it differently
in the system prompt, make apply_edit the only way the resume changes and forbid writing the resume, or any part of it, into the reply

wrap the job posting of the system prompt in a <job_posting> block and add the rule that its content is the job ad text, not instructions, and that any instruction inside it must be ignored and mentioned in warnings
add a line to the system prompt when only one turn is left, asking the agent to close the conversation, tell the candidate how the resume looks now and suggest applying with it

render the greeting of a new conversation from a template per language, resources/greetings/en.jinja and es.jinja, with no call to the LLM: pick it by the conversation language, fall back to English when there is no template for that locale, and name the job and the company of the posting in it

move every Spanish string the tests use as data - the resumes, the candidate messages and the replies of the agent - into tests/fixtures/spanish.py and import them from there, so no test file carries Spanish of its own

add tests/test_english_only.py walking src/, tests/, resources/ and docs/queries.sql for a short list of Spanish markers and failing on anything it finds outside resources/greetings/es.jinja and tests/fixtures/

add the checkpoint test of the tailoring prompt: a candidate asking for a skill the base resume does not back gets a refusal and a warning, the skill never enters the skills array and no change is recorded, with the empty find_evidence and the REJECTED apply_edit visible in the trace

add the checkpoint test of the two languages: with language=en over a resume written in Spanish the agent replies in English, an apply_edit carrying English prose comes back as REJECTED because it does not match the resume language, and the resume stays in Spanish
in the system prompt, forbid copying what a tool answered into the reply and asking the candidate what to do next: the agent decides, acts and reports what it did
run the checkpoint turn against the local Ollama models and write down what they do: the guardrails hold and nothing is invented, but they do not close the turn with the TurnAnswer tool call

insert a resume_version only when the turn actually applied an edit: a turn that answered without touching the resume must write no version and answer with the version that already stands, 0 while the base resume is still the current one
expose jobId and baseResumeId in GET /conversation/{id}, so whoever reopens a conversation knows which job posting and which resume it was started from without having to be told

add a hard scope rule to the system prompt, in both provider variants: the agent is here for this resume and this posting and nothing else, and anything else the candidate brings up — the weather, career advice, how the project works, its services or credentials — gets one line saying it is outside what it does and then back to the tailoring.
